The United States Constitution. The supreme law of the United States, ratified in 1788, establishing the framework of the federal government and defining the rights and powers of the states and citizens. It replaced the Articles of Confederation and created a system of separation of powers across three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial. The Constitution is the world's oldest written national constitution still in use and has been amended 27 times since its inception.

The Constitution is divided into a Preamble, seven Articles, and 27 Amendments. The first ten amendments are collectively the Bill of Rights. Article One establishes Congress, the legislative branch consisting of the Senate and House of Representatives. Article Two establishes the presidency and executive branch. Article Three establishes the federal judiciary, including the Supreme Court. Article Five prescribes the amendment process, requiring a two-thirds majority in both houses of Congress, or a constitutional convention called by two-thirds of state legislatures, and ratification by three-fourths of the states.

The Constitution was drafted at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia in the summer of 1787, presided over by George Washington. The Federalist Papers, essays written by Alexander Hamilton, James Madison, and John Jay, argued for ratification and remain a canonical source for constitutional interpretation. The Constitution was ratified in 1788 and went into effect in 1789, replacing the Articles of Confederation.

The doctrine of separation of powers divides authority among executive, legislative, and judicial branches. Checks and balances allow each branch to limit the power of the others. For example, the Senate confirms judges and cabinet members, the President can veto legislation, and the Court can strike down laws as unconstitutional. The Constitution enshrines federalism: power is shared between the national and state governments. The Tenth Amendment reserves all powers not delegated to the federal government to the states or to the people.
